L'objectif est de répondre au juste besoin des établissements dans des délais de livraison raisonnable, sans rupture d'approvisionnement. --- Forme du contrat : Le marché est un marché de fournitures passé selon la technique d'achat du système d'acquisition dynamique au sens du 4° de l'article L2125-1 du Code de la commande publique. Il est soumis aux dispositions des articles R.2162-37 à R.2162-51 du code de la commande publique. La procédure est entièrement électronique, dès la publication de l'avis de mise en oeuvre du système jusqu'à son expiration. Par nature, le système d'acquisition dynamique est multi-attributaire. Les modalités de remise en concurrence et d'exécution des marchés spécifiques sont prévues à l'article « Marchés spécifiques » du CCAP. Conformément à l'article R2162-41 du code de la commande publique, l'acheteur offre par voie électronique, pendant toute la durée de validité du système, un accès libre, direct et complet aux documents de la consultation. En application de l'article R2162-43 du même code, tout opérateur économique peut demander à participer au système d'acquisition dynamique pendant sa durée de validité

title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source IDIQ contract to Airborne Systems North America, Inc for MMPC Training Services
description: The purpose of this special notice is to provide the Government�s intent to issue a sole source Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract to Airborne Systems North America, Inc. (CAGE 57172), 5800 Magnolia Ave, Pennsauken, New Jersey 08109 for Multi-Mission Parachute Course (MMPC) training services. These services include providing continuous Military Free Fall (MFF) and parachuting training for non-MFF qualified Marines using the designated United States Marine Corps Parachute System-2 (PS-2), in accordance with the approved United States Army Special Operations Command certified MMPC Program of Instruction. Course instruction will ensure successful graduates are qualified to employ the PS-2 during Marine Corps airborne operations. A sole source award will be made on the basis of other than full and open competition under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1(b), Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned is 611699, All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction, with a size standard of $16.5 million. This IDIQ contract will have an ordering period of five (5) years, from 31 March 2027 through 30 March 2032, and will include FAR Clause 52.217-8 with an option to extend the contract for up to six (6) additional months of service. The contract will contain Firm Fixed Price (FFP) line items for years 1 through 5, with an estimated quantity of nine (9) sessions per year and forty-five (45) sessions total. Additionally, the contract will offer a FFP line item for the FAR 52.217-8 option extension, consisting of an estimated four (4) additional sessions. Under these line items, the Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, materials, and facilities to conduct the course in accordance with the Performance Work Statement. The anticipated award date is 31 March 2027. This is not a request for competitive quotes. The Government is not seeking responses to this special notice. The determination not to compete this contract action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses shall be submitted in writing and emailed to the Contract Specialist, Jesse T. Wise at jesse.t.wise.mil@usmc.mil, or the Contracting Officer, Christa Eggleston-Scott at christa.eggleston-sc@usmc.mil.

ACC-RSA is conducting market research on behalf of US Army Transformation and Training Command (T2COM), Combat Capabilities Development Command Aviation and Missile Center (DEVCOM AvMC) to ascertain the capabilities of interested parties in outfitting US Government buildings and/or facilities for Redstone Arsenal, Alabama. title: St. Lucie South Jetty Repair Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 07 December 2026 at 10:00 AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses. This event will provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2027 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $45 million Price Target Range: $25 - $50 million Estimated Period of Performance: 730 calendar days Project Background Project Title: St. Lucie South Jetty Rehabilitation Interagency, Martin County, Florida. Project Description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the head structure of the South Jetty at St. Lucie Inlet. This includes a rebuilt rounded head structure and head-to-trunk transition with a marine mattress foundation and toe protection stones. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking. The reworking of existing stones is only for incorporation of new stone. The retrieval of existing stone outside of the design template will not be required and is not part of the necessary rework of existing stone. The originally constructed South Jetty is approximately 1,320 feet in length with a crest height of 5.5 feet NAVD88. The crest width is 10 feet and the north and south slopes of the structure slope at 1V:2H. There is an asphalt walkway approximately 1,090 feet in length that runs along the existing jetty crest, terminating eastward at approximately Station 12+00 as shown on the approved permit drawings. Manipulation of stone along the crest may be necessary while completing the required work along the side slopes. The asphalt walkway will need to be removed within the repair area as necessary as work progresses. Any asphalt sections removed, or damaged such that they need to be removed, must be transported and properly disposed of off-site, and will not need to be replaced. Project Information Scope of Work: The proposed work includes rehabilitation of the head of the south jetty structure (the seaward-most 400 to 500 feet) by restabilizing the structure foundation and placing a second layer of large armor stone. The proposed scope includes: Excavating the existing bed material to place a widened marine mattress foundation, expanding the current structure footprint up to 85 feet on the jetty centerline as shown on the approved permit drawings; Placing 9- to 15-ton toe protection stones to form the structure foundation and provide scour protection; Removing and disposing of the remaining asphalt walkway and other debris off-site; Repairing the existing core and reworking the single layer of armor stone, as needed; and, Placing a second layer of 9- to 15-ton armor stone to stabilize the structure. Overview of Construction Staging and Access Requirements: Clearing of access routes and staging areas may be required. Any areas that are disturbed during construction are to be restored to pre-construction conditions or better once jetty rehabilitation work is completed. Expansion and/or improvements of access routes may be required. Maximum limits of access routes and staging areas are shown on the approved permit drawings. Additional Environmental Considerations: Construction will be permitted all year round and confined to daylight hours only. Construction that occurs during turtle and shorebird nesting seasons or has the potential to impact other Endangered Species Act (ESA) Protected Species, is subject to environmental restrictions and monitoring requirements. Refer to Table 1 under the Attachments for a list of protected species. Access from the water is allowed, but material cannot be dredged outside of the construction limits. All material excavated must pass through a 2-inch screen prior to use as backfill around the jetty structure or on the beach. All screened material must be disposed of off site. Excavated material may be used to build up the east staging area within the limits shown on the approved permit drawings. After jetty rehabilitation work is complete, the staging area must be graded to the beach fill template and native vegetation restored as shown on the approved permit drawings. Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? Describe the proposed construction methods and equipment needed to rehabilitate the jetty. Address, at a minimum, excavation of existing grade, maintaining open excavation areas, debris removal, and installation of marine mattresses and armor stone. Would temporary earth-retention or water-control measures, such as a cofferdam or similar system, be required to complete the work? Would dewatering be completed if this is the proposed construction methodology? If a cofferdam or other earth-retention system that also excludes all swimming ESA-listed species is not proposed, describe the measures that would be used to prevent the swimming ESA-listed species from entering the active work area during construction, including proposed turtle deterrent measures. ESA-listed species present in the area are included in Table 1 under the Attachments. Describe the turbidity control measures that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If it is not feasible, describe the limitation or restrictions for why not. What safety constraints or hazards could limit the practicality of potential construction methods? What temporary protections or operational measures would be needed to perform the work during winter months, given the inlet�s elevated coastal conditions during that period? Contact Info: Jim LaGrone, Project Manager James.W.Lagrone@usace.army.mil 904-521-2086 If you cannot attend in person: Link Meeting: https://www.microsoft.com/EN-US/MICROSOFT-TEAMS/JOIN-A-MEETING Meeting ID: 993 391 786 289 Passcode: kR3Zt9F8 Join by phone: 601-262-2433 Phone conference ID: 450 517 165# Event Schedule: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above project are invited to submit a capabilities statement, a response to the questionnaire on this Special Notice and any questions you have for the Government ahead of the breakout session by no later than December 04, 2026, at 1:00 PM, EST. All responses under this Special Notice shall be sent via email to Nicole Batista-Cruz at Nicole.M.Batista-Cruz@usace.army.mil, and Ruth Rodriguez at ruth.c.rodriguez@usace.army.mill. Your email subject line should be addressed as "St. Lucie South Jetty Repair Industry Day Registration (Company Name) - W912EP-27-Z-1CUE " to ensure the request is handled in a timely manner. All interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above project are also invited to request a breakout session with the Govern

title: Pre-Solicitation Notice - Clinical East Staffing IDIQ
description: The purpose of this synopsis is to provide notification of the proposed contract action under solicitation number: RFP 7571MN27R00011 for the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Program Support Center (PSC), Federal Occupational Health (FOH) Clinical East Staffing Services. The Government intends to release the solicitation in 1st Quarter Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 through the System of Award Management (SAM.gov) as a Small Business set-aside. The purpose of this requirement is to secure continuing services for occupational health professionals to support Federal Occupational Health (FOH), a component within the Program Support Center (PSC) under the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). FOH defines Occupational Health Services (OHS) as the seamless coordination of comprehensive services using a data-driven approach to assist agencies in achieving a culture of health and high performance. FOH services are designed to improve health outcomes and employee productivity, while reducing occupational health risks, absenteeism, and overall employee health care costs. This requirement is a commercial service and will utilize FAR Part 12/15, as supplemented. The Government intends to issue a single award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) for a period not to exceed five (5) years. Place of Performance: United States of America (USA) East region. This contract will cover work at various FOH Service Provision Sites (SPS) in the FOH Clinical Eastern Region (EAST) including, but not limited to: Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Vermont, West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Puerto Rico. Please do not call or submit questions/inquiries via email, concerning this presolicitation notice. Your interest in this requirement is appreciated.

title: MQ-4C Panel Storage Rack
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division Lakehurst has a requirement to procure Panel Storage Racks, Part Number (P/N) 4106AS0110-1, NSN: 4920-01-655-5582 for the MQ-4C Triton Unmanned Air Systems (UAS) in support of the United States Navy (USN). The Panel Storage Rack provides a temporary storage location for various (R1-R9 and L1-L9) air vehicle access panels when they are removed from the UA. It is used at the organizational level of maintenance for a means to support and store various air vehicle access panels during maintenance on the Triton Unmanned Aircraft inside the hanger. The Government intends to procure the required items under a Small Business Set-Aside competition. It is anticipated that this solicitation will result in a three-year, Firm Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) type contract. See the attached solicitation attachments for further information and instructions.

title: Q702--St. Louis JC Bed Tower IOTA IDIQ
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) October 6, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition and Activation (IOTA) Services for the St. Louis John Cochran Veterans Affairs Medical Center, New Bed Tower. 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal IOTA Services for the St. Louis John Cochran Veterans Affairs Medical Center, New Bed Tower. This requirement supports VA's mission by providing contractor services to help support the activation. The intended contract type is an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with an eight (8) year ordering period. The VA St. Louis Health Care System - John Cochran Division (VA STLHCS-JC), located at 915 North Grand Boulevard, St. Louis, Missouri, is part of a two-division health care system that also includes the Jefferson Barracks VAMC approximately 18 miles south of the John Cochran campus. These facilities serve Veterans in metropolitan St. Louis, Missouri, southwestern Illinois, and the broader Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 15 service area. The John Cochran campus is in a highly constrained urban setting in midtown St. Louis. The existing hospital infrastructure includes Building 1, constructed in 1953, and the Clinical Addition constructed in the mid-1980s. The campus requires modernization to address functional adjacency, physical security/force protection, aging infrastructure, seismic compliance, parking, and clinical capacity concerns. The Department of Veterans Affairs Office of Construction and Facilities Management (CFM), VA St. Louis Health Care System, and the Kansas City District (NWK) U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) are partnering to provide new and replacement facilities for the John Cochran Division. The John Cochran Major Project will relocate inpatient functions to a new seismically compliant Bed Tower, add new functionality, improve departmental adjacencies, replace aging utility infrastructure, and address physical security requirements. The John Cochran Major Project includes campus-wide expansion. Planned new facilities include, but are not limited to, parking garages, a Central Utility Plant, the Bed Tower, an Engineering/Administration building, a motor pool building, and supporting structures. The project includes more than 700,000 net usable square feet of new space. Clinical and administrative services anticipated to be supported include surgery, radiology, pharmacy, surgical services, spinal cord injury inpatient and rehabilitation services, emergency services, engineering, police, nutrition and food services, dialysis, and additional services as refined by the Government-approved program and design documents. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 29 October 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 7 December 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. The first Task Order (TO#1 Project Management and Pre-Planning Support) will be included as part of the solicitation and awarded concurrently with the IDIQ. Quotes will be required for both the IDIQ and Task Order #1. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for quotes. P.O.C: Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

title: Y1DA--NRM-CONST 528-CSI-102 Urology Equipment Site Prep | FY27 NRM
description: The purpose of this project is to renovate two Cystoscopy rooms (214 and 215), Procedure Room (212), Procedure Room (211), Check-In area, Office, Control, Vestibule, Dressing, Toilet and Corridor. The two Cystoscopy rooms (214 and 215) will also receive new medical equipment. The Buffalo VAMC requires a Contractor to perform construction work necessary to accomplish this goal. In addition, Procedure Rooms 212 and 211, a stretch alcove, a check-in area, office, dressing area and restroom are included in this scope of work

title: Renovate Building 1203-DOAS/AHU and Fire Suppression Water System, March Air Reserve Base, California
description: This solicitation is for construction services required for HVAC and Fire Suppression systems repair of Building 1203 at March Air Reserve Base, CA. This is an Invitation For Bid, sealed bid procurement. The solicitation notice will be posted to SAM.gov 4 November 2026 by Close of Business.The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District hereby issues an Invitation for Bid (IFB), Solicitation No. W912QR27BA004, to renovate Building 1203-DOAS/AHU and Fire Suppression Water System, March Air Reserve Base, California. A description of the construction project is as follows:This work consists of, but is not limited to, installing a new Dedicated Outside Air System (DOAS) air handling unit, the replacement of Air Handling Unit (AHU-02) and the replacement of the existing waterline that ties the main waterline to Building 1203. The distance of waterline to be replaced is estimated to be 100-ft. Additional site-work will include a larger housekeeping pad, larger equipment access platform, and larger landscaped enclosure to accommodate the additional DOAS air handling unit. New outside air supply and return ductwork will be incorporated leading from the DOAS unit to the rooms served by AHU-02 providing direct-to-room ventilation. The Contract Duration is 500 calendar days from Administrative Notice to Proceed.TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This IFB is intended to result in the award of one Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction.TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside.DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussion should it be deemed in the be interest of the Government.CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $1 million and $5 million.REGISTRATIONS: Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database: System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. title: St. Lucie South Jetty Repair Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 07 December 2026 at 10:00 AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses. This event will provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2027 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $45 million Price Target Range: $25 - $50 million Estimated Period of Performance: 730 calendar days Project Background Project Title: St. Lucie South Jetty Rehabilitation Interagency, Martin County, Florida. Project Description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the head structure of the South Jetty at St. Lucie Inlet. This includes a rebuilt rounded head structure and head-to-trunk transition with a marine mattress foundation and toe protection stones. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking. The reworking of existing stones is only for incorporation of new stone. The retrieval of existing stone outside of the design template will not be required and is not part of the necessary rework of existing stone. The originally constructed South Jetty is approximately 1,320 feet in length with a crest height of 5.5 feet NAVD88. The crest width is 10 feet and the north and south slopes of the structure slope at 1V:2H. There is an asphalt walkway approximately 1,090 feet in length that runs along the existing jetty crest, terminating eastward at approximately Station 12+00 as shown on the approved permit drawings. Manipulation of stone along the crest may be necessary while completing the required work along the side slopes. The asphalt walkway will need to be removed within the repair area as necessary as work progresses. Any asphalt sections removed, or damaged such that they need to be removed, must be transported and properly disposed of off-site, and will not need to be replaced. Project Information Scope of Work: The proposed work includes rehabilitation of the head of the south jetty structure (the seaward-most 400 to 500 feet) by restabilizing the structure foundation and placing a second layer of large armor stone. The proposed scope includes: Excavating the existing bed material to place a widened marine mattress foundation, expanding the current structure footprint up to 85 feet on the jetty centerline as shown on the approved permit drawings; Placing 9- to 15-ton toe protection stones to form the structure foundation and provide scour protection; Removing and disposing of the remaining asphalt walkway and other debris off-site; Repairing the existing core and reworking the single layer of armor stone, as needed; and, Placing a second layer of 9- to 15-ton armor stone to stabilize the structure. Overview of Construction Staging and Access Requirements: Clearing of access routes and staging areas may be required. Any areas that are disturbed during construction are to be restored to pre-construction conditions or better once jetty rehabilitation work is completed. Expansion and/or improvements of access routes may be required. Maximum limits of access routes and staging areas are shown on the approved permit drawings. Additional Environmental Considerations: Construction will be permitted all year round and confined to daylight hours only. Construction that occurs during turtle and shorebird nesting seasons or has the potential to impact other Endangered Species Act (ESA) Protected Species, is subject to environmental restrictions and monitoring requirements. Refer to Table 1 below for a list of protected species. Access from the water is allowed, but material cannot be dredged outside of the construction limits. All material excavated must pass through a 2-inch screen prior to use as backfill around the jetty structure or on the beach. All screened material must be disposed of off site. Excavated material may be used to build up the east staging area within the limits shown on the approved permit drawings. After jetty rehabilitation work is complete, the staging area must be graded to the beach fill template and native vegetation restored as shown on the approved permit drawings. Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? Describe the proposed construction methods and equipment needed to rehabilitate the jetty. Address, at a minimum, excavation of existing grade, maintaining open excavation areas, debris removal, and installation of marine mattresses and armor stone. Would temporary earth-retention or water-control measures, such as a cofferdam or similar system, be required to complete the work? Would dewatering be completed if this is the proposed construction methodology? If a cofferdam or other earth-retention system that also excludes all swimming ESA-listed species is not proposed, describe the measures that would be used to prevent the swimming ESA-listed species from entering the active work area during construction, including proposed turtle deterrent measures. ESA-listed species present in the area are included in Table 1 above. Describe the turbidity control measures that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If it is not feasible, describe the limitation or restrictions for why not. What safety constraints or hazards could limit the practicality of potential construction methods? What temporary protections or operational measures would be needed to perform the work during winter months, given the inlet�s elevated coastal conditions during that period? Event Date: Monday, 07 December 2026 at 10:00 AM EST Event Location: 2401 SE Monterey Rd, Stuart, FL 34996 *Everyone will need to have a driver's license or id to get through security. title: Architect-Engineering (AE) Indefinite Delivery Contract (IDC) in Support of the Defense Health Agency (DHA) and Component Medical Commands
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT announcement; a market survey for information only, to be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this synopsis or any follow-up information requests. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The purpose of this synopsis is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of various members of industry, to include the Small Business Community: Small Business Firms, SBA Certified 8A Program Participants, SBA Certified Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUB-Zone), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Firms, and Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) Firms. The Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of responsible contractors. Small Business, 8A, HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB are highly encouraged to participate. The type of set-aside decision made will depend upon the capabilities of the responses to this synopsis. I. GENERAL INFORMATION Architect-Engineering (AE) Indefinite Delivery Contracts (IDC) in Support of the Defense Health Agency (DHA) and Component Medical Commands in accordance with FAR 36.6 - Architectural-Engineer Services and Engineering Pamphlet (EP) 715-1-4 - Competing for Architect-Engineer Contracts Awarded by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS): 541330 -- Engineering Services Small Business Size Standard: $25,500,000.00 Standard Industrial Code (SIC): 8711 Engineering Services Product Service Code: C219 Other Architect and Engineering Services Set-Aside: Will Be Determined After the Conclusion of Market Research Anticipated Number of IDC Awards: At least Three (3) IDC Capacity: $9,900,000.00 (Shared Among IDC Awarded) Length of IDC: 5 Years Place of Contract Performance: Various Locations throughout the 48 contiguous United States, and Washington DC (CON US), and Alaska, Hawaii, and US Territories (OCON US) Services would be accomplished at the A-E Firm's Office, with the exception of various Construction Site Services, Field Investigations, and Field Surveys, as required for the individual project. Small Business Firms are Reminded: In accordance with FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, at least 50 percent of the cost of contract performance incurred for personnel shall be expended for employees of the concern. Prior Government contract work is not required for submitting a response under this sources sought synopsis. II. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers - Little Rock District has been tasked to provide multiple Indefinite Delivery Contracts (IDC) in support of the Defense Health Agency (DHA) and Component Medical Commands Medical Sustainment, Restoration and Modernization (MSRM) programs in fiscal years 2027 through 2032. The MSRM program includes replacement, restoration or modernization of active/existing healthcare facilities that include, but are not limited to, clinics, hospitals, medical centers, labs, pharmacies, administrative facilities, ambulatory health facilities, dental clinics, wellness centers, veterinary facilities, vivarium, medical warehouses, and specialty facilities such as hyperbaric chambers, MRI/CT, decontamination facilities, and other facilities and buildings connected to/associated with the Defense Health Agency (DHA) and Component Medical Commands. Specific requirements may include, but are not limited to HVAC, medical gas, plumbing, electrical, elevators, building envelope, fire protection, interior renovation, outfitting, terrorism/force protection, communication, low voltage systems, and exterior site and systems work such as utilities infrastructure, roadways, sidewalks, parking lots, landscaping, and irrigation. The Scope of Work for each of the Task Orders awarded under these IDC will identify outcomes to be satisfied for the specific requirement. At the discretion of the Defense Health Agency (DHA) and Component Medical Commands, contract capacity may be used in support of other USACE customers that may have healthcare facility needs. The IDC may be used throughout the 48 contiguous United States, and Washington DC (CONUS), and Alaska, Hawaii, and US Territories (OCONUS). Services are required to be done by or under the direct supervision of licensed professional Architects or Engineers. The scope of these services includes Planning and Predesign Services (referred to as "AE0" Services); Design-Build (DB) and/or Initial Outfitting (IO) Request for Proposal Development (referred to as "AEl" Services); Design-Build and/or Initial Outfitting (IO) Technical Support Services (referred to as "AE3" Services). Ill. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: Capabilities for programming, planning, and design of healthcare projects in the following areas (examples of support services listed within each of the following functional aspects are representative and not comprehensive). A. Master Planning: Healthcare Planning; Medical Equipment Planning, Space Evaluation and Programming; Military Construction (MILCON) as related to project planning for new medical facilities and related support facilities; as well as Operation and Maintenance (O&M) project planning for expansions and repairs to existing medical facilities and related support facilities. B. Design: Design-Bid-Build Design Services; Engineering, schematic (Charrette) design (10%), concept design {35%), working drawings {65%), and final design (100%); design of expansions and repairs; demolition and alterations to existing medical facilities and related support facilities; and design of new medical facilities and related support facilities to include architectural, comprehensive interior design (CID), space planning; infrastructure systems; and medical equipment plans. Additional design considerations may include, but are not limited to, medical gas systems, fire protection, landscaping, force protection, communication and data design, architectural evaluations, architectural hardware, electronic and communications systems, environmental and EPA regulatory considerations for storm water and site drainage pollution prevention plans; Section 404 Permits and construction site requirements. This work is performed in ongoing active healthcare facilities. A capable and qualified contractor must have experience in performing during the course of normal hospital/clinic operations. C. Assessment/Studies: Identification of code deficiencies; Development of Statement of Conditions and Plans for Improvement for compliance with Joint Commission on the Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations (JCAHO) requirements; Facility Condition Assessments; Environmental Assessments; Economic Analysis of potential projects; Seismic Evaluations; Maintenance and Operational Programming; etc. D. Project Support Services: Construction Phase Services (submittal review, transition planning, commissioning, site visits, etc.); Project Development (preparation of scopes of work, site analysis, assistance with development of draft information for approval documents, etc.); on site Quality Assurance inspections; preparation of reports, record drawings, and other facility documentation; Commissioning plans, performance checklists, systems performance verification testing documentation, specialized quality assurance testing including but not limited to Heating, Ventilation, and Air-Conditioning, plumbing systems, electrical systems, building envelope, acoustic control, integrated automation, communications/data systems, and fire protection systems commissioning; Construction Contractor Schedule Review; Estimating Services; Fire Protection/Life Safety review; Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED)/ Sustainable Design project certification and reporting requirements; LEED preparatory commissioning

Akuuttikorjauksen osa-alueilla vertailuperusteina ovat hinta 95 pistettä ja samaa laitemerkkiä koskevan huoltopalvelun tarjoaminen 5 pistettä. Palveluntuottajia valitaan enintään kaksi per osa-alue. Varsinainen palveluntuottaja ja varasijalle toinen. Mikäli hyväksyttäviä tarjouksia saadaan vain yksi, tilaaja voi perustaa puitejärjestelyn kyseiseen osa-alueeseen yhden toimittajan kanssa. Kaikkia osa-alueita (kaikki jäänhoitokonemerkit) ei tarvitse tarjota. Tuntihintojen ja pisteytyskriteerien tarjoaminen tapahtuu "hankinnat kohdan kriteerit" kohdassa. Huolto- ja tuntihinnat tarjotaan per laitemerkki erikseen. Lisäpisteitä saa, jos samaan merkkiin tarjotaan sekä huolto- että korjauspalvelua. Tällöin korjauspalvelun kohdalla tulee merkitä ”kyllä” tarjottu huoltopalvelua. Tarjottuun hinta on esitettävä arvonlisäverottomina (alv 0 %) nettohintoina, jotka sisältävät kaikki palvelun tuottamisesta aiheutuvat kustannukset mahdolliset kilometri, matka-, majoitus-, päiväraha-, ylityö- sekä toimitus-, laskutus- ja toimistokulut mukaan lukien. Matka-ajasta saa laskuttaa tarjouslomakkeella ilmoitettua tuntihintaa enintään yhdeltä henkilöltä. Matka-aika lasketaan lyhintä tavanomaista ajoreittiä pitkin Oulun kaupungin hallinnolliselta rajalta tai toimittajan Oulun kaupungin alueella sijaitsevasta vakituisesta toimipisteestä työkohteeseen ja takaisin. Erillisiä kilometri-, päiväraha-, majoitus- tai muita matkakuluja ei saa laskuttaa. Mikäli 1. sijoittunut ei pysty /on estynyt ottamasta työtä vastaan, tilaaja käyttää 2. sijoittunutta palveluntarjoajaa. Valittu palveluntuottaja ei voi ilman perusteltua syytä kieltäytyä vastaanottamasta työtilausta ja perustelut annetaan kirjallisesti esim. sähköpostin välityksellä. Huoltopalvelun ja ei-kiireellisen korjauksen vasteaika arkisin on 5 vrk. (työn vastaanotto ja sen aloitus). Akuuttikorjauspalvelun vasteaika arkisin ja viikonloppuisin on 1 vrk. (työn vastaanotto ja sen aloitus). Töitä saavat tilata ainoastaan tilaajan nimeämät yhteyshenkilöt (työnjohtajat), jotka määrittelee erikseen työtä tilatessaan, onko työ huolto- vai ei-kiireellistä tai akuuttikorjaustyötä. Huoltopalvelu suoritetaan merkkivalmistajan huolto-ohjelman mukaisesti ja tarjoajalla tulee olla käytössään merkkivalmistajan tarjoamat ja ylläpitämät diagnostiikkatyökalut tai valmistajan hyväksymät tai teknisesti vastaavat. Huollot toteutetaan pääsääntöisesti kauden ulkopuolella yleensä touko- syyskuun välisenä ajankohtana. Huolto tapahtuu tilaajan tarjoamissa tiloissa Oulun talousalueella (Kanta Oulu, Haukipudas, Kiiminki, Ylikiiminki ja Yli-Ii). Akuuttikorjauspalvelu tehdään tilaajan tilaamana ennalta arvaamattomien vikatilanteiden osalta. Korjaustyö on akuuttia, välitöntä ja välttämätöntä korjausta, johon tulee reagoida sopimuksen mukaisella kiireellisellä aikataululla. Korjaukset tehdään pääsääntöisesti koneiden käyttöpaikalla maastossa. Huolto- ja korjauspalvelussa hankittavien varaosien tulee olla uusia ja alkuperäislaatuisia. Materiaaleille ja varaosille on voimassa kiinteä kateprosentti, joka on 5%. Alkuperäiset varaosien ostolaskut tulee liittää tilaajalle toimitettavaan laskuun mukaan. Tilaajalla on oikeus tarpeen mukaan tilata erikseen yksittäisiä varaosia ja tarvikkeita palveluntuottajalta omaan kalustoon. Tilaaja voi poistaa / lisätä huolto- ja korjauspalvelun piiriin kuuluvaa kalustoa vuosittain. Tilaaja informoi muutoksista palveluntuottajaa. Mikäli Tilaajalle tulee uusia tarjouspyynnössä mainitsemattomia laitemerkkejä, voi tilaaja pyytää puitesopimuskumppaneilta minikilpailutuksen kautta tarjoushinnat uudelle laitemerkille. Tarjoukset eivät saa sisältää omia ehtoja. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu mihinkään hankintamäärään. Tilaajalla on oikeus hylätä kaikki tarjoukset perustellusta syystä. Die tatsächlichen während der Vertragslaufzeit erfolgenden Beauftragungen können hinsichtlich der in einem Fachlos enthaltenen Bedarfsmengen der jeweiligen Versorgungsnummern abweichen. Die Obergrenze für den jeweiligen Auftrag bildet in jedem Fall die in dem betreffenden Fachlos zusammengefasste Gesamtmenge (Schätzbedarf + Sicherheitszuschlag). Eine Verpflichtung des AG, Einzelaufträge zu erteilen, wird durch diesen Vertrag nicht begründet. Die Vertragslaufzeit beginnt mit Zuschlagserteilung und endet am 31.12.2030. Des Weiteren behält sich der Auftraggeber eine optionale Verlängerung der Rahmenvereinbarung bis zum 31.12.2033 vor. Wenn der bestehende Vertrag zwischen der HIL GmbH und der Bundeswehr, egal aus welchem Rechtsgrund endet, kann die Rahmenvereinbarung durch ein Sonderkündigungsrecht beendet werden.

Ter dekking van mogelijke onvoorziene kosten is bij de raming een marge van 50% toegepast, wat resulteert in een plafondbedrag van €2.700.000 (exclusief btw) voor de gehele looptijd van de Opdracht. Voor de werking van de raamovereenkomst en het plaatsen van nadere opdrachten wordt verwezen naar paragraaf H2.8. title: Flight System Team Systems Integration and Technical Expertise
description: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) has a requirement for a four-month extension to contract 80MSFC24CA012 for engineering skills, manpower, and technical capability needed by the Flight Systems Team within the Human Exploration Development and Operation Chief Engineer�s Office within the Engineering Directorate. The tasks involved with this work cover all phases of ongoing vehicle systems integration and testing, as well as design support for future mission planning efforts. In addition, this contract also provides specialized technical engineering expertise, as well as ground and on-orbit test support, for proprietary flight platforms. The required support involves access to proprietary vehicle design information, interface documentation, and anomaly resolution data. Resolution, LLC personnel currently possess the necessary access, knowledge, and integration history to analyze and apply this information without interruption to ongoing operations. NASA MSFC intends to issue a sole source contract modification to acquire these services from Resolution, LLC for an additional four (4) months through April 30, 2027, under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.� Pursuant 6.103-1, Resolution�s team serves in a Chief Engineer advisory capacity and provides critical technical oversight and independent engineering assessment throughout the platform lifecycle. NASA/MSFC has maintained a dedicated government-led team, consisting of both civil servants and contractor personnel, in continuous support of this program since 1999. With over more than two decades of support, the team has developed unique institutional knowledge, specialized analytical tools, and mission-specific expertise necessary to track and resolve vehicle anomalies; document design, test, and operational issues; capture and apply lessons learned; implement systems engineering best practices; monitor and assess flight performance data; support launch, ascent, on-orbit, recovery, and post-flight operations; and provide engineering recommendations to inform vehicle modifications, upgrades, and future mission planning. Resolution, LLC maintains a workforce with demonstrated experience supporting vehicle anomaly resolution, certification activities, interface verification, and operational engineering functions specific to the platform. The continuity of this highly specialized support is essential to maintaining mission effectiveness, preserving program knowledge, and ensuring the timely identification and resolution of technical issues affecting vehicle performance, reliability, and operational success. NASA/MSFC requires continued contract support under the current contract 80MSFC24CA012 beyond its current period of performance end date to continue providing systems engineering, integration, interface, verification, and certification support. The required support activities include Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System (TDRS) requirements decomposition, legacy TDRS compatibility assessment, interface closure, demonstration planning, and technical preparations necessary for the commercial Ka band demonstration and transition to operations. These activities must continue without interruption to meet mission schedules and transition milestones. This extension will allow for uninterrupted services while NASA/MSFC assesses the results of market research and utilizes that information to continue with an appropriate procurement strategy. This work is within the existing scope of Contract 80MSFC24CA012 and represents a continuation of ongoing systems engineering, integration, interface management, verification, and certification support currently being performed by Resolution, LLC. Failure to execute this continuation would result in unnecessary schedule impacts and increased technical, integration, and programmatic risk associated with transition and loss of critical knowledge. Accordingly, Resolution, LLC is the only responsible source capable of providing the required services within the necessary time frame and with acceptable risk to the Government. The Government does not intend to acquire a commercial item using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Cynthia Hubbard at Cynthia.a.hubbard@nasa.gov, alternate contact Annette.Hawkins@nasa.gov no later than 10:00 am CST on Monday, December 7, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at : https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf

title: USACE SPK DBB Construction - Calaveras Wastewater Treatment Plant Improvements - Copperopolis, CA
description: This Sources Sought Notice is being issued for market research purposes to determine the availability, capability, and interest of small business firms for a potential Government requirement. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE; requests for the solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) anticipates a potential requirement for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) construction services to conduct Copper Cove Wastewater Treatment Plant (CCWTP) Improvements in collaboration with the Calaveras County Water District (CCWD) in Calaveras County, California (CA). The project is anticipated to include installation of a new continuous backwash filtration system to replace an existing filter system; electrical improvements to include upgrading the existing PG&E service size to the main switchboard located in the Control Building, installing a new transformer, raceways, metering panel, new Motor Control Center (MCC), and associated wiring and components; interconnection with a pre-existing CCWD-installed suspended air floatation (SAF) filter pretreatment system; installation of a new continuous backwash filter system to include excavation, shoring, and backfill for a partially buried cast-in-place concrete tank with three (3) equipped filter cells (modules), air control panel, grating and handrailing over the filter cells and feed channel; inlet and outlet piping, valves, and connection to existing ultraviolet (UV) inlet piping; and power and control tie-ins. The project is also anticipated to include construction of a new masonry compressor building on a concrete slab foundation, housing a duplex air compressor with space for an additional unit, along with appurtenant equipment on the compressed air piping including a refrigerated air dryer, oil-water separator, and air filter; a new wet well and submersible pump station to include a new buried precast wet well with an adjacent valve vault housing a duplex submersible pump station, valves and appurtenances, piping, and power control conduits constructed adjacent to the new SAF to convey filter backwash waste flow to the SAF. Finally, the project is anticipated to include demolition and disposal of the existing adsorption clarifier and mixed media filter equipment, dewatering of sludge handling facility solids in three (3) containerized, polymer-assisted gravity sludge dewatering systems that will be positioned on a concrete pad with containment walls and drainage systems to capture drained water and return it to Pond 6 through three (3) quick coupler hose connection points (one (1) per bin), and all associated yard pipe modifications to connect the new components to the existing WWTP, generally buried in suitable native or engineered backfill at depths of approximately three (3) to ten (10) feet of cover. The potential requirement may result in a firm-fixed-price construction solicitation issued approximately December 2026. If solicited, the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by approximately March 2027. The Government estimates that construction of the anticipated requirement can be completed within three-hundred-sixty-five (365) calendar days from Contractor receipt of the Notice to Proceed. Work may also be impacted by bird nesting season, which runs from 1 February through 31 August. If market conditions indicate the estimated period of performance may be unrealistic, Respondents are encouraged to provide specific information (such as known equipment lead times or other timeline concerns) for Government consideration when responding to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government currently estimates the target price range for the anticipated project may be between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code identified for the anticipated requirement is 237110, Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction. The small business size standard for the NAICS, as established by the U.S. Small Business Administration, is $45,500,000.00 annual revenue. The Product or Service Code (PSC) for the anticipated requirement is Y1PD, Construction of Waste Treatment and Storage Facilities. If there is a reasonable expectation that two (2) or more responsible small business concerns under the NAICS can provide the anticipated services, the Contracting Officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. If competition is set-aside for competition limited to small businesses, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (Deviation), requires that construction small business Contractors self-perform at least twenty-five percent (25%) of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. If no set aside is made, the requirement is competed with full and open competition, and the awarded Contractor is not a small business, the Contractor may be required to self-perform a percentage of work if required in the solicitation. Contractors with the skill, capabilities, workload capacity, and ability to obtain bonding to complete the project described above (either through self-performance and/or Subcontractor management) are invited to provide capability statements to the primary point of contact listed below. Other than small businesses are also encouraged to submit Capability Statements. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Responses must be limited to ten (10) 8.5 x 11 inch pages with a minimum font size of point 10. Please provide the following information: 1) Company name, System for Award Management (SAM) Unique Entity Identification (UEID) number or Employer Identification Number (EIN), address, point of contact name, contact phone number, contact e-mail address, and statement identifying whether the company employs union or non-union workers. 2) Experience and capability to complete contracts of similar magnitude and complexity to the potential requirement, including at least three (3) examples of comparable work performed within the past six (6) years. Each example should include a brief description of the project, description of the work performed (identification of self-performance and/or Subcontractor management), customer name, customer satisfaction, timeliness of performance, dollar value of the project, and whether there were any challenges experienced during the project (delays, investigations, health and safety issues, labor shortages, management / organizational issues, etc.). 3) Business size and socioeconomic type for the applicable NAICS (ex: Woman-Owned Small Business, Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), certified Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), 8(a) Participant, small business, or other than small business (large business)). 4) Bonding capability (in the form of a Surety letter). Please submit all capabilities statements, information, brochures, and/or marketing material as one (1) document, limited to the page quantity above. Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may result from this Notice. Moreover, responses will not restrict the Government to an acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted or the capability statements received. Please provide responses and/or questions by e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Costa Laliotitis, at (Constantinos.Laliotitis@usace.army.mil) by 0800 / 8:00 a.m. Pacific Time on Monday, 7 December 2026. Please include the Sources Sought Notice number W9123827X1CHG in the e-mail subject line.

description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT Notice Number: NIH-NOI-27-PCA-NIAID-12580 Posted Date: November 25, 2026 Response Due Date: December 7, 2026 Classification Code: 6640 � Laboratory Equipment and Supplies NAICS Code: 811210 � Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance 1. Agency and Contracting Activity Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) National Institutes of Health (NIH) National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Division of Intramural Research (DIR) Laboratory of Viral Diseases (LVD) For: Section of Barrier Immunity Building 33, Room 1E05 33 North Drive Bethesda, MD 20892 Project Number: PCA-NIAID-12580 Project Title: Service Contract for BD Symphony S6 (Base Plus Two Option Years) 2. Action Being Announced This is a notice of intent, and not a request for competitive quotations, proposals, or bids. The National Institutes of Health (NIH), on behalf of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-price sole source contract to: BD Biosciences, Inc. 2350 Qume Drive San Jose, CA 95131 USA for a service contract to provide preventive maintenance, emergency repair service, replacement parts, labor, travel, software revisions, and technical support for the BD Symphony S6 Flow Cytometer, serial number R66293700030, including associated lasers, for a base year and two option years. 3. Statutory Authority The Government intends to award this requirement on a sole source basis pursuant to: 41 U.S.C. 152(3), 41 U.S.C. 1901, and FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), soliciting from a single source for purchases at or below the simplified acquisition threshold, as applicable. This sole source determination is based on the conclusion that only one source is capable of providing the services required at the level of quality required because the services are unique and highly specialized. 4. Description of Requirement The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), Division of Intramural Research (DIR), Laboratory of Viral Diseases (LVD), Section of Barrier Immunity, requires a service contract for the BD Symphony S6 Flow Cytometer, serial number R66293700030, and five associated lasers. The required service coverage includes, at a minimum: For the BD Symphony S6: Two (2) preventive maintenance inspections during each contract year, including PM kits; Guaranteed 48-hour response to requests for emergency on-site service; Software revisions released during the agreement term; Unlimited on-site service visits Monday through Friday; and Unlimited telephone support for instruments, reagents, and applications at no additional charge. For the five associated lasers: G4 355-60 w/BD UV SAPPHIRE 488-400 Blue MPB 532-1000 SORP Green MPB 628-1000 .3mm Red SORP OBIS 405-100 LX Violet The required service coverage includes: Unlimited service visits Monday through Friday; and Repair or replacement as needed. The anticipated period of performance is January 5, 2027 through January 4, 2030, inclusive of a base year and two option years. The total estimated value of the requirement, including options, is $250,840.80. 5. Background The Section of Barrier Immunity within the Laboratory of Viral Diseases conducts research to better understand the mechanisms of HIV/SIV disease progression and to facilitate therapeutic interventions aimed at decreasing microbial translocation and disease progression. The laboratory conducts research on the NIH intramural campus and collaborates with scientists in academic and clinical laboratories nationwide. A major focus of the Section is the study of cellular HIV/SIV infection in various primate models throughout disease progression and in the context of therapeutic treatments. To study distinct cellular subsets within these models, the laboratory relies extensively on flow cytometric cell analysis for a majority of its research experiments and studies. The BD Symphony S6 Flow Cytometer was purchased in March 2021 at a cost of $723,265.70 and has been in daily use since that time. Because the instrument is highly sensitive and technically complex, regular preventive maintenance and prompt repair service are essential to ensure reliable operation and continuity of research. Failure to maintain or repair the instrument quickly would negatively impact ongoing studies and jeopardize the Government�s investment in both the equipment and the associated research resources. 6. Sole Source Determination In accordance with FAR Part 10 and applicable HHS acquisition guidance, market research was conducted for this requirement. Market research included: review of required sources; review of Federal Supply Schedules; review of NIH strategic sourcing resources; review of commercial websites and product literature; application of personal knowledge in procuring similar services; contacting knowledgeable individuals in Government and industry regarding market capabilities; participation in online communications among industry, acquisition personnel, and customers; and obtaining source information from other contracting activities, agencies, and commercial sources. The market research determined that BD Biosciences is the only vendor capable of providing the required service coverage for this instrument at the level of quality required. Specifically, BD Biosciences is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the BD Symphony S6 and is the only source identified that can provide: OEM-certified service by factory-trained technicians with specialized knowledge of the BD Symphony S6 platform; guaranteed access to OEM replacement parts, components, and modules; software revisions compatible with the instrument throughout the agreement term; unlimited on-site service visits; unlimited telephone support; and a guaranteed 48-hour emergency response time. Additionally, BD Biosciences confirmed on November 24, 2026 that it is the only vendor authorized to perform maintenance on its equipment. Accordingly, no other source is known that can satisfy the Government�s requirement without unacceptable risk to instrument performance, research continuity, and data integrity. 7. Procurement History This is a follow-on requirement for continued service coverage of the BD Symphony S6 Flow Cytometer. Previous Contractor: BD Biosciences Previous AMBIS Sequence Number: 2250157 Current AMBIS Sequence Number: 2275750 Initial and subsequent awards competed: Yes The instrument has been covered by service contracts since its original procurement in 2021. 8. Responses from Interested Sources This notice is not a solicitation. However, any responsible source that believes it is capable of meeting the Government�s requirement may submit a capability statement for consideration. Interested parties must demonstrate, through clear and convincing documentation, their ability to provide service support equivalent to that described in this notice for the BD Symphony S6 Flow Cytometer and associated lasers. Capability statements shall include, at a minimum: company name and address; description of the vendor�s authorization to service the BD Symphony S6; evidence of access to OEM parts, components, and software revisions; documentation demonstrating ability to provide a guaranteed 48-hour on-site response time; description of technician qualifications and training specific to the BD Symphony S6 platform; and explanation of how the vendor will meet each of the Government�s minimum requirements. Responses must be received no later than December 7, 2026. description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT Notice Number: NIH-NOI-27-PCA-NIAID-12762 Posted Date: November 25, 2026 Response Due Date: December 7, 2026 Classification Code: 6640 � Laboratory Equipment and Supplies NAICS Code: 811210 � Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance 1. Agency and Contracting Activity Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) National Institutes of Health (NIH) National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Division of Intramural Research (DIR) Laboratory of Viral Diseases (LVD) For: National Institutes of Health NIAID/LVD Building 33, Room 1E05 33 North Drive Bethesda, MD 20892 Project Number: PCA-NIAID-12762 Project Title: Service Contract for CytoFLEX SRT 2. Action Being Announced This is a notice of intent, and not a request for competitive quotations, proposals, or bids. The National Institutes of Health (NIH), on behalf of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-price sole source contract to: Beckman Coulter, Inc. 5350 Lakeview Parkway South Drive Indianapolis, IN 46268 for a one-year service contract to provide preventive maintenance, repair coverage, OEM parts, labor, travel, priority response, phone support, engineering modifications, and operator training for the CytoFLEX SRT, serial number BF32140. 3. Statutory Authority The Government intends to award this requirement on a sole source basis pursuant to: 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) and FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), soliciting from a single source for purchases at or below the simplified acquisition threshold, as applicable; Under simplified acquisition procedures, contracting officers may solicit from one source when circumstances deem only one source reasonably available This sole source determination is based on the conclusion that only one source is capable of providing the services required at the level of quality required because the services are unique and highly specialized. 4. Description of Requirement The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), Division of Intramural Research (DIR), Laboratory of Viral Diseases (LVD), requires a one-year service contract for the CytoFLEX SRT, serial number BF32140. The required service coverage includes, at a minimum: One (1) preventive maintenance inspection during the period of performance by a Beckman Coulter-authorized and factory-certified technician; Coverage for repair, OEM parts, labor, and travel; Priority response and telephone support; Engineering modifications supported by genuine new parts; and Additional key operator training during regular service visits. The anticipated period of performance is January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027. The total estimated value of the requirement is $43,635.00. 5. Background Research programs in the Laboratory of Viral Diseases (LVD) explore fundamental aspects of cell and molecular biology, viral pathogenesis, and viral immunology within the context of a diverse group of medically important viruses, including human/simian immunodeficiency viruses, poxviruses, herpesviruses, papillomaviruses, coronaviruses, influenza viruses, alphaviruses, and flaviviruses. The goals of these research programs are to increase basic biological understanding of these pathogens and their interactions with their hosts and to generate new strategies for preventing and treating viral diseases. This equipment is used by the Single Virion Biology & Biophysics Unit in the Laboratory of Viral Diseases. The research program broadly focuses on uncovering fundamental molecular mechanisms of virus translocation across cell membranes. The CytoFLEX SRT flow cytometer and cell sorter is essential to pursuing the research objectives of the Ivanovic laboratory. The CytoFLEX SRT is used to detect and measure traits and sort cell and virion populations from research projects investigating the morphology of influenza virions and other aspects of influenza biology. The instrument is located on the NIH main campus in Building 33, Room 1E19, Bethesda, Maryland. 6. Sole Source Determination In accordance with FAR Part 10 and applicable HHS acquisition guidance, market research was conducted for this requirement. Market research included: application of personal knowledge in procuring similar services; contacting knowledgeable individuals in Government and industry regarding market capabilities; participation in online communication among industry, acquisition personnel, and customers; obtaining source lists from other contracting activities, agencies, trade associations, and other sources; and reviewing catalogs and generally available product literature published by manufacturers, distributors, and dealers or available online. The Scientific Operations Manager reviewed required sources, Federal Supply Schedules, NIH strategic sourcing resources, and commercial websites and determined that only Beckman Coulter offers the required level of OEM service support for the CytoFLEX SRT. Specifically, Beckman Coulter was the only source identified that can provide: unlimited guaranteed OEM replacement service parts, components, or modules necessary for repairs; priority response on-site service; unlimited telephone support; compatible software revisions; engineering modifications supported by genuine new parts; and additional key operator training throughout the agreement term. The CytoFLEX SRT is specialized for the detection of small virus particles and sorting of infectious populations, unlike other flow cytometers that function primarily at the larger cellular level. The instrument includes specialized lasers and resolution capabilities necessary to detect and sort individual virions as required by the research projects in the Single Virion Biology & Biophysics Unit. Only Beckman Coulter provides the necessary specialized supplies and manufacturer-authorized service support for the CytoFLEX SRT, and only Beckman Coulter-trained technicians possess the expertise required to maintain the instrument in proper working order while preserving manufacturer support. Accordingly, no other source is known that can satisfy the Government�s requirement without unacceptable risk to instrument performance, research continuity, and data integrity. 7. Procurement History This requirement is for continued service support of the CytoFLEX SRT. Procurement History: The instrument transferred to LVD in 2021 and has been covered by service contracts since that time. Previous Purchase Orders: LAW2135976, 75N93023P00156, and associated option years Current AMBIS Sequence Number: 2309556 8. Responses from Interested Sources This notice is not a solicitation. However, any responsible source that believes it is capable of meeting the Government�s requirement may submit a capability statement for consideration. Interested parties must demonstrate, through clear and convincing documentation, their ability to provide service support equivalent to that described in this notice for the CytoFLEX SRT, serial number BF32140. Capability statements shall include, at a minimum: company name and address; description of the vendor�s authorization to service the CytoFLEX SRT; evidence of access to OEM parts, components, software revisions, and engineering modifications; documentation demonstrating ability to provide priority response on-site service; description of technician qualifications and factory certification specific to the CytoFLEX SRT platform; and explanation of how the vendor will meet each of the Government�s minimum requirements. Responses must be received no later than December 7, 2026. title: Flight System Team Systems Integration and Technical Expertise
description: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) has a requirement for engineering skills, manpower, and technical capability needed by the Flight Systems Team within the Human Exploration Development and Operation Chief Engineer�s Office within the Engineering Directorate. The tasks involved with this work cover all phases of ongoing vehicle systems integration and testing, as well as design support for future mission planning efforts. In addition, this contract also provides specialized technical engineering expertise, as well as ground and on-orbit test support, for proprietary flight platforms. The required support involves access to proprietary vehicle design information, interface documentation, and anomaly resolution data. Resolution, LLC personnel currently possess the necessary access, knowledge, and integration history to analyze and apply this information without interruption to ongoing operations. NASA MSFC intends to issue a sole source contract modification to acquire these services from Resolution, LLC. under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.� Pursuant 6.103-1, Resolution�s team serves in a Chief Engineer advisory capacity and provides critical technical oversight and independent engineering assessment throughout the platform lifecycle. NASA/MSFC has maintained a dedicated government-led team, consisting of both civil servants and contractor personnel, in continuous support of this program since 1999. With over more than two decades of support, the team has developed unique institutional knowledge, specialized analytical tools, and mission-specific expertise necessary to track and resolve vehicle anomalies; document design, test, and operational issues; capture and apply lessons learned; implement systems engineering best practices; monitor and assess flight performance data; support launch, ascent, on-orbit, recovery, and post-flight operations; and provide engineering recommendations to inform vehicle modifications, upgrades, and future mission planning. Resolution, LLC maintains a workforce with demonstrated experience supporting vehicle anomaly resolution, certification activities, interface verification, and operational engineering functions specific to the platform. The continuity of this highly specialized support is essential to maintaining mission effectiveness, preserving program knowledge, and ensuring the timely identification and resolution of technical issues affecting vehicle performance, reliability, and operational success. NASA/MSFC requires continued contract support under the current contract 80MSFC24CA012 beyond its current period of performance end date to continue providing systems engineering, integration, interface, verification, and certification support. The required support activities include Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System (TDRS) requirements decomposition, legacy TDRS compatibility assessment, interface closure, demonstration planning, and technical preparations necessary for the commercial Ka band demonstration and transition to operations. These activities must continue without interruption to meet mission schedules and transition milestones. This extension will allow for uninterrupted services while NASA/MSFC assesses the results of market research and utilizes that information to continue with an appropriate procurement strategy. This work is within the existing scope of Contract 80MSFC24CA012 and represents a continuation of ongoing systems engineering, integration, interface management, verification, and certification support currently being performed by Resolution, LLC. Failure to execute this continuation would result in unnecessary schedule impacts and increased technical, integration, and programmatic risk associated with transition and loss of critical knowledge. Accordingly, Resolution, LLC is the only responsible source capable of providing the required services within the necessary time frame and with acceptable risk to the Government. The Government does not intend to acquire a commercial item using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Cynthia Hubbard at Cynthia.a.hubbard@nasa.gov, alternate contact Annette.Hawkins@nasa.gov no later than 10:00 am CST on Monday, December 7, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at : https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf
