description: THIS NOTICE IS FOR SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR INVITATION FOR BID. SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS AND DRAWINGS ARE NOT AVAILABLE. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Respondents will not be notified of the Sources Sought results. This Sources Sought is issued for the sole purpose of conducting Market Research in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 10 and identifying vendors capable of fulfilling Agency needs. USACE personnel may contact firms responding to this announcement to clarify a responder�s capabilities and other matters as part of this market research process. The tracking number for this announcement is W912P827SSA001. Please include in your firm�s response to this Sources Sought request. USACE anticipates a requirement under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330, Engineering Services. The Government contemplates and unrestricted procurement with a reserve for Small Business concerns for a Firm Fixed Price Multiple Award Task Order Contracts (MATOC) for MVN Civil Works Program & Project Management Support Services. The requirement: USACE New Orleans District seeks responsive and responsible small business offerors who shall provide services for the Civil Works Program & Project Management Support Services for efforts related to the water resources programs in southern Louisiana including USACE Civil Works Programs. Services include project management/planning support, development of project performance reports, updates to program management plans, project scheduling input, project cost support, presentation development, interagency agreement development /updates, project drawings and maps, other project reports, and monthly status reports. Qualifications: The contractor shall have the capability of providing project management and planning support, development of project performance reports, updates to Project/Program Management Plans (PMPs), project scheduling analysis, project cost tracking support, development of project performance reports, project cost tracking support, development of briefings and presentations, interagency agreement support, mapping and spatial project visual support, and monthly contract status reports. The contractor shall formulate flood risk management, navigation, and ecosystem restoration plans supported by quantitative benefits analysis. The contractor shall conduct studies, inventory and forecast of problems and opportunities, formulation of measures and alternative plans, evaluation and comparison of alternatives plans, evaluation and comparison of alternatives, calculation and comparison of monetized and non-monetized benefits. The contractor shall prepare documents such as federal interest determination, reconnaissance, feasibility, post-authorization and other reports, including cultural resources studies and reports, and hazardous, toxic, and radiological waste (HTRW) investigations, National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and /or other environmental quality documents. The contractor shall document water and wastewater issues as necessary to develop master plan level documents for environmental infrastructure, PAS, SJ, CAP, and other programs as required. The contractor shall develop ecosystems habitat surveys, endangered or threatened species surveys, wetlands assessments using standard State of Louisiana methods in coopetition with other Federal and State agencies, modeling, and mitigation and monitoring plans. The contractor shall coordinate with Corps, non-Federal partners, and other stakeholders to document existing flood damage problems, historical flood maps, potential ecosystem restoration, and recreation problems and opportunities within the study area. The contractor shall coordinate with Corps and non-Federal partners to document required excavation permits, utility easements, rights-of-way, and other project-related requirements shortly after exercising this contract. The contractor shall document all or part of NEPA and/or other environmental documents, including, but not limited to, Biological and HTRW assessments, Environmental Assessments (EA), and Environmental Impact Statements (Els's). Potential sources are requested to submit: A Capability statement identifying current or previous contracts, scope and magnitude of Program & Project Management Support Services. Please note: All contractors doing business with the Federal Government must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. The website for registration Potential firms MUST have an active record in the System for Award Management (SAM) database to be considered for award. Include in your capabilities package: your company's name, address, Point of Contact with corresponding phone number, e-mail address, Unique Entity Identifier Number, Cage Code, and System for Award Management profile which displays the expiration date. Proof of small business size must also be included. All interested firms are invited to submit a capability statement of no more than five (5) pages back and front, and no smaller than 12-point Times New Roman font. The capability statement should demonstrate the interested firm's understanding, capability, approach, qualifications, and past experience as it relates to the work stated within this Source Sought notice. Please note that a small business firm may submit a capability statement that includes the expertise of large business partner companies under a teaming arrangement. If a teaming arrangement is contemplated, then the response to this Sources Sought must clearly discuss the tasks that the small business firm intends to perform; and the specific areas that the large business teaming partner intends to perform. Please note that at least 51% of the total cost of all services provided must be incurred by or for personnel of the small business firm or a similarly situated entity, pursuant to Revolutionary FAR overhaul (RFO) clause 52.219-14 entitled "Limitations on Subcontracting". Responses to this Sources Sought may be submitted electronically to the following e-mail address: amy.c.feemster@usace.army.mil. No hard copies, facsimile submissions, or telephone responses will be accepted. All interested firms with 541330 as an approved NAICS code have until Monday, December 7, 2026, at 11:00AM (CST) to submit their capabilities package. Submissions that are not received within the allotted time specified will not be considered.

title: 6515--NX EQ Sterilizer Unit Low Temperature H2O2 (VA-27-00018787)
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Enterprise Procurement Office (EPO), formerly the Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a means of conducting market research to identify qualified sources with the capability and resources to meet the Veterans Health Administration s (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program requirement for Sterilizer Unit Low Temperature H2O2, with 3D printed items sterilization capabilities. The EPO in conjunction with VHA is seeking qualified sources capable of supplying the Steris Corporation® V-Pro Max 2 Sterilizer or equivalent products that satisfy the Salient Characteristics on an agency-wide basis. VA is contemplating the award of a single Requirements Contract with Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) orders IAW FAR 16.503, Requirements Contracts, to a supplier of this equipment. Respondents will be required to deliver complete Steris Corporation® V-Pro Max 2 Sterilizer to VA medical centers and facilities throughout the United States. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 339113 Surgical Appliance and Supplies Manufacturing and the associated size standard is 800 employees. The FAR Provision found at 52.204-7 requires that The Offeror shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer or quotation. You may access the SAM website at SAM.gov | Home. All respondents must be certified with the appropriate NAICS code on the SAM website. All Service Disable Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) / Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) respondents must be verified in the SBA database at: https://www.sba.gov/veterans/#vetcert at the time of submission. Submissions for this Sources Sought Notice shall be submitted by email no later than December 9, 2026, at 12:00pm Eastern Time to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer at the following email addresses: Joseph.Jeranek@va.gov Kimberly.LeMieux@va.gov Email responses shall include the following subject line: Response to Sources Sought Notice 36C10X27Q0031. This notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted as a result of this notice. This notice is part of a continuous process for obtaining the latest information on the commercial status of the industry with respect to their current and near-term abilities. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for, or award, a competitive contract. It is emphasized that this is a notice solely for planning and informational purposes. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. The Government may or may not issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. There is no solicitation available at this time. 2.0 SCOPE OF WORK The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program has identified the Sterilizer Unit Low Temperature H2O2, with 3D printed items sterilization capabilities, as a candidate for a Veterans Affairs (VA)-wide (otherwise referred to as national ) single Requirements contract award. The Low Temperature, Gaseous Plasma, Vaporized Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2), Sterilizers are used for low temperature sterilization of heat and moisture-sensitive medical devices. Hydrogen peroxide is a known antimicrobial agent that oxidizes key cellular components within microorganisms, thereby destroying them. A low-temperature gaseous plasma sterilizer is an apparatus that uses vaporized hydrogen peroxide gas plasma to sterilize heat- and moisture-sensitive medical instruments and devices. The process involves injecting hydrogen peroxide vapor into a chamber, then applying an electrical field to create gas plasma. This plasma generates microbicidal free radicals that disrupt cellular components of microorganisms, killing them effectively. The process leaves behind harmless byproducts, water and oxygen, and is suitable for delicate equipment that cannot withstand high temperatures or humidity. Sterilization typically occurs at a temperature of less than 56°C with process times of around 25 to 70 minutes depending upon cycles type. title: Rare Language Interpreter Services
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Rare Language Interpreter Services Background This Sources Sought (Request for Information (RFI)) ONLY, is to determine whether there are interested, capable, and qualified organizations in the marketplace with the knowledge, skills, qualifications, capacity, and capability to meet the Government's obligations herein. The primary mission of the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) is to adjudicate immigration cases by fairly, expeditiously, and uniformly interpreting and administering the Nation�s immigration laws. Under delegated authority from the Attorney General, EOIR conducts immigration court proceedings, appellate reviews, and administrative hearings. EOIR�s Language Services Unit (LSU) manages and coordinates language interpretation services for immigration court proceedings. EOIR employs an internal workforce of federal employee staff interpreters. EOIR also contracts with several interpretation service companies (as opposed to contracting directly with individual interpreters) to utilize contract interpreters when staff interpreter coverage is not available. The Language Services Unit (LSU) of Rare Languages Interpreters has a requirement to utilize contract interpreter services for rare languages when current conventional interpreter services are not readily equipped or available.Services will be both in-person and virtual. Your organization is invited to provide a capability statement for rare language services. All responses are confidential. Attached is a listing of the rare languages that we have encountered and expect to run across in the future where rare language interpreters will need to be readily accessed. title: Request for Information (RFI) Enhanced Maritime Biological Detection (EMBD) Identification Subsystem (IDS)
description: The Joint Product Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Sensing (JPdM CS), under the Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Integrated Early Warning (JPM CBRN IEW), under the Portfolio Management Executive Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (PME CBRND) within the Department of War (DoW), is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of providing a Biological Warfare Agent (BWA) identification capability for integration into the U.S. Navy's Enhanced Maritime Biological Detection (EMBD) system. USACE anticipates a requirement under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330, Engineering Services. The Government contemplates and unrestricted procurement with a reserve for Small Business concerns for a Firm Fixed Price Multiple Award Task Order Contracts (MATOC) for MVN Civil Works Program & Project Management Support Services. The requirement: USACE New Orleans District seeks responsive and responsible small business offerors who shall provide services for the Civil Works Program & Project Management Support Services for efforts related to the water resources programs in southern Louisiana including USACE Civil Works Programs. Services include project management/planning support, development of project performance reports, updates to program management plans, project scheduling input, project cost support, presentation development, interagency agreement development /updates, project drawings and maps, other project reports, and monthly status reports. Qualifications: The contractor shall have the capability of providing project management and planning support, development of project performance reports, updates to Project/Program Management Plans (PMPs), project scheduling analysis, project cost tracking support, development of project performance reports, project cost tracking support, development of briefings and presentations, interagency agreement support, mapping and spatial project visual support, and monthly contract status reports. The contractor shall formulate flood risk management, navigation, and ecosystem restoration plans supported by quantitative benefits analysis. The contractor shall conduct studies, inventory and forecast of problems and opportunities, formulation of measures and alternative plans, evaluation and comparison of alternatives plans, evaluation and comparison of alternatives, calculation and comparison of monetized and non-monetized benefits. The contractor shall prepare documents such as federal interest determination, reconnaissance, feasibility, post-authorization and other reports, including cultural resources studies and reports, and hazardous, toxic, and radiological waste (HTRW) investigations, National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and /or other environmental quality documents. The contractor shall document water and wastewater issues as necessary to develop master plan level documents for environmental infrastructure, PAS, SJ, CAP, and other programs as required. The contractor shall develop ecosystems habitat surveys, endangered or threatened species surveys, wetlands assessments using standard State of Louisiana methods in coopetition with other Federal and State agencies, modeling, and mitigation and monitoring plans. The contractor shall coordinate with Corps, non-Federal partners, and other stakeholders to document existing flood damage problems, historical flood maps, potential ecosystem restoration, and recreation problems and opportunities within the study area. The contractor shall coordinate with Corps and non-Federal partners to document required excavation permits, utility easements, rights-of-way, and other project-related requirements shortly after exercising this contract. The contractor shall document all or part of NEPA and/or other environmental documents, including, but not limited to, Biological and HTRW assessments, Environmental Assessments (EA), and Environmental Impact Statements (Els's). The Government may or may not issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. There is no solicitation available at this time. 2.0 SCOPE OF WORK The Low Temperature, Gaseous Plasma, Vaporized Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2), Sterilizers are used for low temperature sterilization of heat and moisture-sensitive medical devices. Hydrogen peroxide is a known antimicrobial agent that oxidizes key cellular components within microorganisms, thereby destroying them. A low-temperature gaseous plasma sterilizer is an apparatus that uses vaporized hydrogen peroxide gas plasma to sterilize heat- and moisture-sensitive medical instruments and devices. The process involves injecting hydrogen peroxide vapor into a chamber, then applying an electrical field to create gas plasma. This plasma generates microbicidal free radicals that disrupt cellular components of microorganisms, killing them effectively. The process leaves behind harmless byproducts, water and oxygen, and is suitable for delicate equipment that cannot withstand high temperatures or humidity. Sterilization typically occurs at a temperature of less than 56°C with process times of around 25 to 70 minutes depending upon cycles type. title: NOTICE OF INTENT: DIRECT NEGOTIATED SALE OF SURPLUS FEDERAL VESSEL EX-VADM K.R. WHEELER (T-AG-5001) FOR OPERATIONAL COMMERCIAL RE-USE
description: UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION MARITIME ADMINISTRATION OFFICE OF SHIP DISPOSAL PROGRAMS (MAR-640) � WASHINGTON, D.C. 20590 NOTICE OF INTENT: DIRECT NEGOTIATED SALE OF SURPLUS FEDERAL VESSEL EX-VADM K.R. WHEELER (T-AG-5001) FOR OPERATIONAL COMMERCIAL RE-USE Notice Type Special Notice / Notice of Intent Primary Statutory Authority 46 U.S.C. � 57102; 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2) Proposed Disposition Action Direct Negotiated Commercial Re-Use Sale (Sales Contract MA-14564) Proposed Purchaser To Be Disclosed Upon Execution Pursuant to Statutory Requirements This is a notice of intent, not a request for a quotation or competitive proposal. A solicitation document will not be issued, and quotations, bids, or proposals will not be requested or accepted. 1. Statutory Authority and Action Summary The United States Department of Transportation, Maritime Administration (MARAD), acting by and through the Office of Ship Disposal Programs (MAR-640), pursuant to 46 U.S.C. � 57102 and 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2), hereby provides public notice of its intent to execute Sales Contract No. MA-14564 for the direct negotiated sale and transfer of title of the surplus National Defense Reserve Fleet (NDRF) vessel Ex-VADM K.R. WHEELER (T-AG-5001), IMO No. 9354038, for operational commercial re-use at a purchase price matching or exceeding the government's verified Fair Market Value appraisal. This disposition is conducted pursuant to MARAD�s primary maritime vessel disposal authorities under 46 U.S.C. � 57102 and the national security negotiated disposal exemption under 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2), independent of standard General Services Administration (GSA) competitive auction mechanisms. Conveyance of title and delivery shall occur strictly from MARAD custody at the Beaumont Reserve Fleet (Beaumont, TX) on an "AS IS, WHERE IS" basis. 2. Asset Identification and Condition Government Asset Designation Ex-VADM K.R. WHEELER (T-AG-5001) IMO / Registry Number IMO No. 9354038 Current Custody & Location Beaumont Reserve Fleet (Beaumont, TX) / Inactive NDRF Fleet Primary Technical Capabilities Offshore Petroleum Distribution System (OPDS) platform equipped with specialized dynamic positioning systems, deep-water fluid discharge apparatus, and high-volume pumping infrastructure. Conveyance Terms Conveyed strictly "AS IS, WHERE IS" with full buyer indemnification and mandatory post-closing hull biofouling and towing remediation obligations. Appraised Fair Market Value At or above verified Fair Market Value (established by formal appraisal from the Office of Shipyards & Marine Engineering). 3. Statutory Framework and Primary Considerations for Direct Negotiated Disposition Pursuant to 46 U.S.C. � 57102, 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2), and 41 CFR � 102-38.105(e), the Maritime Administration has determined that a direct negotiated sale of the Ex-VADM K.R. WHEELER for operational commercial re-use best serves national security, statutory directives, and the public interest based upon the following core determinations: Preservation of Critical National Security Infrastructure (OPDS): The Ex-VADM K.R. WHEELER was uniquely constructed as the primary operational platform for the Offshore Petroleum Distribution System (OPDS), capable of delivering bulk petroleum products to military forces in austere or degraded maritime environments. Commercial re-use and transfer into the U.S. Flag commercial fleet ensures the private-sector reactivation and maintenance of these specialized logistics systems, preserving strategic surge capability for U.S. Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM) and Military Sealift Command (MSC) at zero ongoing federal expense. Proprietary Technical and Engineering Data Compliance: Safe reactivation, United States Coast Guard (USCG) certification, and sustained commercial operation of the vessel require lawful access to specialized technical data, original build schematics, and proprietary dynamic positioning intellectual property. Direct negotiation ensures transfer to an entity demonstrating verified proprietary data rights and operational capacity to achieve Coast Guard compliance without government indemnification. Statutory and Regulatory Defense Covenants: The conveyance contract requires enforceable covenants running with the vessel, including U.S. documentation restrictions under 46 CFR Part 221, a statutory 10-year foreign trade restriction surety bond pursuant to 46 U.S.C. � 57102, and prohibitions against unauthorized foreign transfer, re-flagging, or premature scrapping. Elimination of Federal Liabilities and Fund Recovery: Direct disposition terminates ongoing layberth, hull maintenance, security, and environmental compliance overhead, while net proceeds are statutorily deposited into dedicated maritime accounts under 46 U.S.C. � 57103 to support NDRF operations and training programs. 4. Public Notice Information and Inquiries This posting is published for public transparency and statutory reporting awareness. As a non-competitive negotiated disposition under 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2) and 46 U.S.C. � 57102, no solicitation will be released and no bids, capability statements, or quotations are solicited. description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF) Contracting Department (Code 400) Requirement: Confidence Testing, Inspection, and Certification of ANSUL Automatic CO2 Fire Suppression System Document / PR Number: N4523A12956436 1. GENERAL INFORMATION & NOTICE DISCLAIMER THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. THIS NOTICE IS ISSUED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR INVITATION FOR OFFERORS TO SUBMIT PROPOSALS. A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION WILL BE POSTED AT A LATER DATE WHICH WILL PROVIDE INSTRUCTIONS FOR OFFERORS TO RESPOND TO THIS OPPORTUNITY. The Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF), Contracting Department (Code 400), is issuing this sources sought notice. The sources sought is being issued as a means of conducting market research to determine the interest, availability, and capability of Industry to participate in a competitive acquisition for semi-annual confidence testing, inspection, certification, emergency trouble calls, and repair services for an ANSUL Automatic CO2 Fire Suppression System protecting an industrial plant varnish dip tank system in Building 427 at PSNS & IMF, Bremerton, WA. The tentative North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code selected for this acquisition is 561621 (Security Systems Services - Fire Alarm Systems Sales/Installation/Servicing), , with an applicable Small Business Size Standard of 25.0M (for NAICS 561621). To be considered an interested vendor, your company should possess the applicable NAICS code in your System for Award Management (SAM) profile. Interested offerors must be active and registered in SAM at www.sam.gov. Based on the responses received to this sources sought notice, this requirement may be set-aside for small business (in full or in part), procured through full and open competition (unrestricted), or procured on a sole-source basis. All small business set-aside categories (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business [SDVOSB], and Women-Owned Small Business [WOSB]) will be considered. Telephonic inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged. The Government will not provide evaluations, debriefs, or formal comments to companies providing sources sought responses; however, the responses received will be used to inform the Government as to the best means of procuring this requirement. FURTHER SPECIFICATIONS AND DETAILS WILL BE PROVIDED IN THE FORTHCOMING REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) OR REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS (RFQ). 2. SUMMARY OF REQUIREMENT & SCOPE OF WORK Objective: The Contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and non-personal services to perform semi-annual confidence testing, inspection, and certification on an ANSUL Automatic CO2 Fire Suppression System, as well as handle emergency trouble calls and unscheduled repairs. Protected Equipment: The system protects critical industrial plant equipment (varnish dip tank system) supporting the dipping and coating of electric motor components in Shop 51. Scheduled and potential emergent fleet support requires the system to maintain a state of continuous operational readiness. Place of Performance: Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & IMF, 1400 Farragut Ave, Bremerton, WA 98314, Building 427, at Column 34. Period of Performance: Semi-annual service for a base period of one (1) year with options up to a total of five (5) years (anticipated execution window: June 2027 through June 2032). Core Tasks & Frequencies: Scheduled Maintenance: Semi-annual onsite confidence testing and complete inspection (at 6-month intervals). Coordination requires a 20-business-day lead time to request and approve system outages. System inspection includes detectors, agent release/manual pull stations, audible/visual devices, CO2 storage containers, actuator functionality, signal verification to the monitoring station, battery voltage/standby power transfer, and operational/safety training for personnel as requested. Emergency Trouble Calls: Provision of up to two (2) emergency trouble calls per contract year. The Contractor must be capable of providing emergency service 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and responding on-site within twenty-four (24) hours of notification. Includes up to eight (8) hours of on-site service, associated travel, and up to $200 in minor repair parts/materials. Unscheduled Inspection & Repair: On-call non-emergency repairs and fault corrections identified between scheduled maintenance visits (ordered as firm-fixed-price task orders not to exceed $20,000 across the ordering period). Reporting & Deliverables: Submission of comprehensive Service Reports within forty-eight (48) hours of visit completion, documenting compliance with NFPA 12, operational status, test results, and any required follow-on recommendations. Deliverables conform to Data Item Description DI-NDTI-80809 (CDRL A001). 3. MANDATORY CONTRACTOR SPECIAL QUALIFICATIONS & SECURITY REQUIREMENTS Interested parties must demonstrate their ability to meet the following mandatory prerequisites: NICET Certification: Personnel performing inspection, testing, and certification must possess a current National Institute for Certification in Engineering Technologies (NICET) certification in Special Hazards Systems (Level II or above). ANSUL OEM Training & Authorization: The Contractor must be formally trained and certified by ANSUL to design, install, test, and maintain carbon dioxide fire suppression systems. The Contractor must also be an authorized ANSUL stocking distributor of clean agent/special hazards equipment to ensure immediate availability of replacement parts from inventory. CO2Recharging Facility Access: The Contractor must maintain or have direct access to a carbon dioxide recharging station located within fifty (50) miles of Puget Sound Naval Shipyard, capable of recharging the complete system within twenty-four (24) hours following a discharge event. Security Clearance & Badging: Contractor personnel performing work must possess a valid NAVSEA Green Badge at the time of proposal submission and maintain access throughout contract performance. Work is subject to shipyard security controls in accordance with DD Form 254. Applicable Codes & Standards: Full compliance with NFPA 12 (Standard on Carbon Dioxide Extinguishing Systems), NFPA 72 (National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code), 29 CFR 1910, 29 CFR 1915, and PSNS&IMF Occupational Safety and Health Manual OSH-II-9 (Lockout/Tags-Plus). 4. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS (CAPABILITY STATEMENT) Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement addressing the criteria below: Company Information: Company Name, Address, and Website. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone Number, and Email Address). Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number and CAGE Code. Socioeconomic Business Size/Status under the identified NAICS code (e.g., Small Business, HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, Large Business). Technical Qualifications & Capabilities: Confirmation of employee(s) possessing NICET Level II (or higher) in Special Hazards Systems. Verification of authorized ANSUL stocking distributor status and technician ANSUL certification for CO2 systems. Location of the CO2 recharging facility within 50 miles of PSNS & IMF and demonstration of 24-hour post-discharge recharge capability. Demonstration of capability to provide 24/7 emergency dispatch with on-site response within 24 hours. Confirmation that designated personnel currently possess or are eligible to immediately receive a NAVSEA Green Badge. Relevant Past Experience: Brief summary of up to three (3) relevant projects completed within the past five (5) years demonstrating similar experience with industrial CO2 fire suppression system maintenance, testing, and certification. title: Request for Information (RFI) Enhanced Maritime Biological Detection (EMBD) Identification Subsystem (IDS)
description: The Joint Product Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Sensing (JPdM CS), under the Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Integrated Early Warning (JPM CBRN IEW), under the Portfolio Management Executive Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (PME CBRND) within the Department of War (DoW), is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of providing a Biological Warfare Agent (BWA) identification capability for integration into the U.S. Navy's Enhanced Maritime Biological Detection (EMBD) system. As a backward-compatible replacement for the Joint Biological Point Detection System (JBPDS) Identifier, the EMBD Identification Subsystem (IDS) automatically provides confirmatory identification of Biological Warfare Agents (BWAs) in liquid samples. In operation, the EMBD Collector gathers the sample externally and routes it to the IDS via the EMBD Fluid Transfer System (FTS). Please see the attached formal Request for Information (RFI) for full details. Responses to questions have been attached via word document; "Request For Information (RFI)_EMBD_Identification Subsystem (IDS) Questions."

title: Department of War Pharmacy Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreement/Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program
description: The Department of War (DoW) is required by law (10 U.S.C. � 1074g) to establish an effective, efficient, integrated pharmacy benefits program for the Military Health System (MHS) which includes the purchase pharmaceutical agents. Prior to the scheduled P&T Committee meeting, a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for pharmaceutical agents within Drug Classes identified for placement on the UF has been issued to obtain quotes from industry. title: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for (3) dredging projects. The areas of consideration for these dredging services are: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor. Calcasieu River Bar Channel: Work for the Calcasieu River Bar Channel will require one fully crewed and equipped self-propelled trailing suction type hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -45ft MLLW and place dredged material into the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Sites (ODMDS).Pascagoula Harbor: Work for the Pascagoula Harbor maintenance dredging will require a hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -46 ft MLLW and place dredged material in the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS). Dredged material shall be placed within Pascagoula ODMDS. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within 3-5 miles of the dredge cut. Panama City Harbor: Work for the Panama City Harbor maintenance dredging will require a medium to small hopper. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -40 ft MLLW and place dredged material within channel adjacent to the entrance jetty. Dredged material shall be placed within the channel adjacent to the jetty. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within one mile of the dredge cut. The Contractor shall commence dredging no later than 30 January 2027 in Calcasieu River Bar Channel. The order of work is as follows: (1) Calcasieu River Bar Channel, (2) Pascagoula Harbor, (3) Panama City Harbor. This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 23 October 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the size standard is $37,000,000.00. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) in order to be eligible to receive an award from any Government solicitation. Call 1-866-606-8220 for more information or visit the SAM website at www.sam.gov. After completing SAM, in order to download documents contractors and their subcontractors must register at www.sam.gov. In order to locate solicitation, Contractors can go to www. sam.gov and search for the solicitation number. Contractors can register to be put on a plan holders list that others can access through the www.sam.gov website. It is the Offerors responsibility to check the Internet address provided as necessary for any posted changes to this solicitation and all amendments. For additional information or assistance, please contact Cori Caimi, Contract Specialist, email cori.a.caimi@usace.army.mil or Rosalind Shoemaker, Contracting Officer, phone (910) 251-4436, email rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil.

title: 99 CS Commercial TV over IPTV
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, following RFO 12.201-1 Simplified Procedures, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Government reserves the right to award without discussions or to make no award at all depending upon (1) the quality of quotes received and (2) whether proposed prices are determined to be fair and reasonable.1. The solicitation number is FA486127Q0002. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP). A Firm Fixed Price type contract will be awarded.2. The incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01, effective 13 March 2026.3. This combined synopsis/solicitation is being issued as a Full and Open Competition, and the associated NAICS code is 517111 - Wired Telecommunications.4. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform installation, maintenance, and delivery of High-Definition (HD) local and cable television programming to designated areas of the facility. Service must be fully compatible with the Governments existing hardware, specifically the Haivision Play 2000-C Set-Top Box, for use with the Haivision IPTV Media Platform or as a stand-alone solution. This Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) establishes an enterprise-wide commercial television solution for Nellis Air Force Base. It encompasses the following cost components:Line of Effort (LOE) 1 (Core Headend Feed): A central IPTV multi-channel feed delivered directly to Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE) Haivision Encoders, managed by the 99th Communications Squadron. Line of Effort (LOE) 2 (Decentralized Endpoint Services): Monthly fee per active television connection, to be utilized by the 99 ABW Command Post and other authorized tenant units via separately funded Call Orders. Premium Channels: Monthly subscriptions for additional premium programming channels, as requested by authorized units.Initial Setup / Stream Configuration: A one-time activation, installation, and programming configuration charge (if applicable).Pricing Instruction: Offerors shall submit their pricing using Attachment 2 - Price List (Fillable PDF). Offerors must input their proposed monthly costs for LOE 1, LOE 2, and Premium Channels, and their one-time cost for Initial Setup. The quantities are locked at 12 months (for recurring items) and 1 each (for one-time items) to establish a standardized 12-month Total Evaluated Price (TEP) baseline for evaluation. description: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. IAW RFO 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. SOURCES SOUGHT DESCRIPTION This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a sources sought/RFI only. The purpose of this sources sought/RFI is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS 513210 (size standard of $47 Million). Responses to this sources sought will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this sources sought, a solicitation announcement may be published. Responses to this sources sought synopsis are not considered adequate responses for a solicitation announcement. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), HSA 5.3 Network Contracting Office, is seeking sources that can provide an Electronic Quality Management Software System that at a minimum meets the attached Statement of Work with a brand name or equal. Electronic Quality Management Software System STATEMENT OF WORK Scope The desired service is required for an electronic Quality Management web-based software platform for quality management of HSA 5.3 Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Service (PLMS). Modules requested are: Document Control Competency Assessment Non-Conforming Event Management Training Program Inspection Preparedness tools capable of supporting checklist management through methods permitted by each accreditation agency s licensing agreements. CAP checklists may only be used in accordance with CAP intellectual property policies. Services to be provided include complete software set up and configuration, conversion from previous formats, onsite or web-based training, software upgrades, and ongoing client support. QMS Software Requirements. Access The software must provide unlimited (24/7/365) access for approximately 700 -1000 unique user profiles. Software allows for multiple users to be assigned to different permissions/roles as needed by facility. Users can be assigned multiple permissions and roles within software. Operational Features Must include software upgrades for new versions of the software including updates to the current version. Software must be compatible with the VA available browser that VHA subscribes to (currently Chrome version 142.x, Or Microsoft Edge version 142.x) Additional supporting software or plug-ins that are required to be installed (including new versions) on VA owned hardware in order to operate the system properly must be on the VA Technology/Standard List. 99% annual operational uptime of system. Backup solution including an off-site, live fail-over server which can be activated within a short time in case of catastrophic failure. Data must be exportable in non proprietary formats (e.g., CSV, XML, PDF) to meet VA Records Management requirements in the event the company ceases operations or at the completion of the contracted time. Technical Features Solution must be a commercially off the shelf product that is available for full installation within 30 days of the award. Solution must be FedRAMP Moderate (or higher) authorized and must obtain and maintain a VA Authority to Operate (ATO) prior to production use. The software must have the ability to allow access to multiple users at multiple sites simultaneously. Must be web based. Ability to connect into our active directory for log in and email functions. System must be compatible with a PIV (Personal Identity Verification) card, 2 factor authentication login system. If solution offered is deemed to be SaaS, vendor complies with all VA security requirements for hosting documents as specified containing User Identifiable, business critical information. Have workflows and documents organized and managed by division/site; available across enterprise (all sites within V22 PLMS). The system must be compliant with all Office of Information and Technology and Information Security directives. The contractor s performance must be in compliance with all applicable state, federal and local laws and regulations. If the product is to be installed on VA equipment on the VA system, the solution/product supplied by the contractor must be approved in the VA Technical Reference Model (TRM) prior to use or installation. https://www.oit.va.gov/Services/TRM/TRMHomePage.aspx. If the contractor provides direct remote support within the VA system, the contractor must obtain a VA Interconnection Security Agreement (ISA) and complete all required VA security documentation (e.g., SSP, PTA/PIA) in support of ATO without impacting installation timeframes in section 5 Upgrade/Updates The Contractor shall provide updates to both the equipment hardware and software in order to maintain the integrity of the system and the state-of the art technology, at no additional charge to the Government. These shall be provided as they become commercially available and at the same time as they are being provided to commercial customers. This requirement only applies to system updates that enhance the model of equipment being offered, i.e. new version of software, correction of software defect, update offered to commercial customers at no additional charge, upgrade to replace model of equipment no longer Contractor supported, etc. This does not refer to replacing the original piece of equipment provided under the IDIQ; however, it does refer to significant changes in the hardware operational capability. Document Control Software must have the ability to handle over 50,000 documents. Software must allow customizable templates which may include headers, footers, and numbering. Software must allow various types of documents (File formats) to be used within the system, such as, but not limited to Word, PDF, Excel, VISIO, and PowerPoint. Software must allow multiple approvers on a single document. Software must allow documents to be linked to other documents within the system. Document editing and audit of changes must be contained within the software package. Version/change control with change audit available (so you can see what changes were made) Documents can be tagged to more than one laboratory department and or location. Ability for users to submit a change (edit) request on a live document. Bank of available template and reports to monitor user compliance. Ability to export reports into PDF, Word, and Excel. Capability to reassign documents when someone leaves. Can transfer ownership and approvals of documents if employee transfers. Allows for transfer of roles and responsibilities without reapproval of documents. Allows for addition and removal of staff from groups and assigned documents. Ability of document not being published immediately after approval. Allows for delay in publication of documents after approval to allot time for training needs. A minimum of 5 permission levels: Level 1 (i.e. Administrator) Multiple users will be assigned this role per each facility as needed. Level 2 (i.e. Medical Director) Approval of documents Level 3 (i.e. Owner) access to create, edit and all other features needed for the document lifecycle. Level 4 (i.e. Writers ) access to create, edit and other features needed for document lifecycle Level 5 (i.e. General Users) access to read and acknowledge documents applicable to assigned duties. title: Y1BG--FY27 NRM - EHRM Base 630-22-700 EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades - Manhattan VAMC
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC), is conducting a market survey and seeking potential sources for the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades Construction Project at the Margaret Cochran Corbin VA Campus in New York, NY. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This project will provide infrastructure upgrades required to support the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) system at the Margaret Cochran Corbin VA Campus in New York, NY. Located within a dense, landlocked urban block, the medical center presents significant logistical and coordination challenges, including constrained access, deliveries, staging, hoisting, worker parking, material storage, and exterior work near existing flood barriers. The scope includes relocation and construction of a new campus data center; renovation of 53 telecommunications rooms and enclosures; installation and certification of Category 6A cabling, data outlets, horizontal pathways, and patch panels; campus-wide fiber upgrades, redundant fiber pathways, and WAN pathway improvements; normal and emergency electrical distribution upgrades, including grounding, bonding, and 2N uninterruptible power supply and downstream electrical distribution redundancy for the data center; dedicated cooling and mechanical system upgrades supporting critical IT infrastructure, including a standalone chilled water system designed for continuous, year-round operation and ductless fan coil units serving telecommunications spaces; fire alarm and suppression upgrades, including clean-agent provisions, early detection, supervised controls, emergency lighting, and emergency power and HVAC shutoffs within the data center; physical security improvements; rooftop equipment protection and enclosures; selective demolition and construction; restoration of interior finishes; civil coordination; and hazardous material abatement. The relocated data center will function as the campus telecommunications hub and will require carefully sequenced construction, system testing, equipment migration, and cutover activities to maintain uninterrupted healthcare operations. Work will be performed in occupied healthcare facilities located in Buildings 1, 2, 3, and 6 and will require phased construction, controlled access, and close coordination with clinical departments, VA Information Technology personnel, station space committees, project teams, third-party service providers, and other ongoing station construction projects. Renovation of the 53 telecommunications rooms and enclosures will require phased access throughout the occupied buildings and coordination of room-size and equipment requirements to meet Infrastructure Standards and Technology Services (ISTS) requirements. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price construction contract utilizing the design-bid-build delivery method (final specifications and drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued either as a Request for Proposals (RFP) in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 15, considering technical and price factors, or as an Invitation for Bids (IFB) in accordance with RFO Part 14, considering price only. The results of this market research will assist the Government in determining the final procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information obtained during the market research process. The anticipated solicitation is currently planned for release in February 2027. The magnitude of construction is between $40,000,000.00 and $50,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 236220 (size standard $45.0 million) applies to this procurement. The anticipated period of performance is 960 calendar days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The contractor will provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and other resources necessary to complete the project in accordance with the contract documents prepared by an independent architect-engineer firm. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide the company name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, point-of-contact name, telephone number, and email address. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 236220. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, HUBZone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAPM Magnitude of Construction listed above. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: No more than three (3) contracts that your company has performed within the last seven (7) years that are of comparable size, complexity, and scope to this requirement. Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates. Provide specific examples that relate aspects of previous projects to the proposed project. Describe specific technical skills and key personnel your company possesses to perform the requirements described under description of work. Describe your Self-Performed** effort (as either a Prime or Subcontractor). Describe Self-Performed work in terms of dollar value and description. **Self-Performed means work performed by the offeror themselves, NOT work performed by another company for them for any of the project examples provided. Section 6: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) - A PLA is defined as a pre-hire Collective Bargaining Agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C. 158(f). The PLA questionnaire must be filled out and returned with the Sources Sought response. The questionnaire can be found at the end of this document. description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, following RFO 12.201-1 Simplified Procedures, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Government reserves the right to award without discussions or to make no award at all depending upon (1) the quality of quotes received and (2) whether proposed prices are determined to be fair and reasonable.1. The solicitation number is FA486127Q0002. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP). A Firm Fixed Price type contract will be awarded.2. The incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01, effective 13 March 2026.3. This combined synopsis/solicitation is being issued as a Full and Open Competition, and the associated NAICS code is 517111 - Wired Telecommunications.4. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform installation, maintenance, and delivery of High-Definition (HD) local and cable television programming to designated areas of the facility. Service must be fully compatible with the Governments existing hardware, specifically the Haivision Play 2000-C Set-Top Box, for use with the Haivision IPTV Media Platform or as a stand-alone solution. This Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) establishes an enterprise-wide commercial television solution for Nellis Air Force Base. It encompasses the following cost components:Line of Effort (LOE) 1 (Core Headend Feed): A central IPTV multi-channel feed delivered directly to Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE) Haivision Encoders, managed by the 99th Communications Squadron. Line of Effort (LOE) 2 (Decentralized Endpoint Services): Monthly fee per active television connection, to be utilized by the 99 ABW Command Post and other authorized tenant units via separately funded Call Orders. Premium Channels: Monthly subscriptions for additional premium programming channels, as requested by authorized units.Initial Setup / Stream Configuration: A one-time activation, installation, and programming configuration charge (if applicable).Pricing Instruction: Offerors shall submit their pricing using Attachment 2 - Price List (Fillable PDF). Offerors must input their proposed monthly costs for LOE 1, LOE 2, and Premium Channels, and their one-time cost for Initial Setup. The quantities are locked at 12 months (for recurring items) and 1 each (for one-time items) to establish a standardized 12-month Total Evaluated Price (TEP) baseline for evaluation. Offerors shall not alter the locked quantities or pre-programmed formulas in Attachment 2 - Price List. Submit offers via email to riley.finn@us.af.mil

title: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for (3) dredging projects. The areas of consideration for these dredging services are: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor.Calcasieu River Bar Channel: Work for the Calcasieu River Bar Channel will require one fully crewed and equipped self-propelled trailing suction type hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -45ft MLLW and place dredged material into the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Sites (ODMDS).Pascagoula Harbor: Work for the Pascagoula Harbor maintenance dredging will require a hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -46 ft MLLW and place dredged material in the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS). Dredged material shall be placed within Pascagoula ODMDS. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within 3-5 miles of the dredge cut.Panama City Harbor: Work for the Panama City Harbor maintenance dredging will require a medium to small hopper. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -40 ft MLLW and place dredged material within channel adjacent to the entrance jetty. Dredged material shall be placed within the channel adjacent to the jetty. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within one mile of the dredge cut. The following will be the performance periods:Calcasieu River Bar Channel: 15 January 2027 to TBDPascagoula Harbor: 01 April 2027 to 30 September 2027Panama City Harbor: 01 August 2027 to 30 September 2027This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 23 October 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the size standard is $37,000,000.00. description: Project Title: Department Of Energy - National Nuclear Security Administration Joint Cyber Facility Project Location: Building 810, Denver Federal Center, Lakewood, Colorado 80225 NAICS: 236220, Commercial & Institutional Building Construction Estimated Price Range: Between $10 and $20 million 1. Project Summary: The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), intends to procure construction services for a design-bid-build project for the development of a Joint Cyber Facility (JCF) for the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) at the Denver Federal Center in Lakewood, Colorado. This requirement for a new turnkey JCF consists of approximately 23,688 square feet of combined office and support space, including approximately 16,000 square feet of finished office workspace and 7,688 square feet of existing mechanical and electrical rooms supporting the space. The project includes integration of existing equipment from a prior data center installation. The finished space includes a reception area, offices, conference rooms, hoteling cubicles, pantry, server room, and a large video conferencing room. Construction and tenant build-out will occur within an occupied facility, necessitating careful coordination with active surrounding tenants. Work includes, demolition, architectural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, telecommunications, audio visual system infrastructure, security infrastructure, equipment, and coordinating installation of system furniture components, all of which must strictly adhere to accreditation requirements and standards. 2. title: Sources Sought Synopsis: Repair of NSN: 5840-01-659-4499
description: Notice Type: Sources Sought Synopsis 1. Notice This is not a solicitation, but rather a Sources Sought Synopsis to determine potential sources. This request is for information and planning purposes only. The purpose of this Sources Sought Synopsis is to conduct market research to determine if responsible sources exist; to assist in determining if this effort can be competitive, and/or a total Small Business Set-Aside. The proposed North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) Code is 811210, which has a corresponding Size standard of $34M in average annual receipts. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement. The Government is interested in all small businesses to include 8(a) Small Business Development Programs, Service-Disabled Veteran- Owned, Historically Under-utilized Business Zone(s) (HUBZone), and Women-Owned small business concerns. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this notice and identify your small business status relative to the identified NAICS code above. Additionally, please provide any anticipated teaming arrangements, along with a description of similar services offered to the Government and to commercial customers for the past three years. Any responses involving teaming agreements should delineate between the work that will be accomplished by the prime, and the work accomplished by the teaming partners. 2. Description Requirement Name: Repair of NSN: 5840-01-659-4499 For the end item, the contractor shall furnish all facilities, parts, materials, equipment and services required to inspect and, if necessary, restore to serviceable condition. The Government does not own the data or the rights to the software/data needed to purchase/repair this part through additional sources. It has been determined to be uneconomical to buy the data or rights to the data. It is uneconomical to reverse engineer the part. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM): APPLIED SYSTEMS ENGINEERING INC CAGE: 3Z966 ADDRESS: 7510 Benbrook PKWY Benbrook, Texas 76126-2112, United States 3. Statement: Authority: 10 U.S.C. 2304(C)(1), Justification: Supplies required are available from only one or a limited number of responsible sources and no other type of supplies will satisfy agency requirements. This part requires engineering source approval by the design control activity in order to maintain the quality of the part. Existing unique engineering skills, and repair knowledge by the qualified source(s) require repair of the part by the approved source(s). The approved source(s) retain repair knowledge, or technical data that are not economically available to the Government, and the data or knowledge is essential to maintaining the quality of the part. An alternate source must qualify IAW the design control activity's procedures, as approved by the cognizant Government engineering activity. The qualification procedures must be approved by the Government engineering activity having jurisdiction over the part in the intended application. The Government does not own the technical data to provide contractors for qualification. 4. Anticipated Procurement Details Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Period of Performance: 320 Days ARO 5. Capability Statement Submission Requirements Interested parties possessing the requisite capabilities are invited to submit a Capability Statement addressing the criteria outlined below. Business Information: Provide the following business information for your company: Company Name Address Point of Contact CAGE Code Phone Number E-mail Address Web Page Address Specify whether your company is a U.S. or foreign-owned firm Recommended North American Industry Classification System (NAICS Code) if other than 811210 Based on the above NAICS code, state whether your company is a small business and provide additional information regarding the type of small business (women-owned, small- disadvantaged, HUB Zone, etc.). Potential Offeror Capabilities: What is your experience in providing the capability to accomplish the objective/requirements listed above? Include contract numbers, a brief description of the work performed, period of performance, agency/organization supported, and individual points of contact (Contracting Officers or Program Managers). Provide pricing data, to include historical pricing data if available. How would the prime contractor account for government furnished property (GFP) in the possession of the prime, and all sub-contractors? Does your company currently have any teaming agreements in place that will allow for successfully meeting the Government's requirements? In addition, please identify the roles associated with the teaming arrangement. Discuss any documents or data you will require to complete the objectives listed above, and briefly explain their purpose. What are the top five risks you see in accomplishing this effort? How long would it take you to submit a proposal? Provide other relevant topics, concerns, or information not addressed in this posting. 6. Response Procedures Submission Format: Electronic format only (PDF preferred) Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed five (5) pages Due Date & Time: In accordance with (IAW) the date published on SAM.GOV Delivery Method: Submit via email to the points of contact on SAM.GOV 7. Disclaimer This is a Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) issued in accordance with FAR Part 10 (Market Research) and FAR 15 (Contracting by Negotiation). This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). Nothing in this document shall be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice, nor will it reimburse any costs incurred by interested parties in preparing or submitting responses. All information received in response to this notice marked "Proprietary" will be handled accordingly. The Government reserves the right to use non-proprietary information provided in market research reports, acquisition strategy determinations, and procurement development.

title: Y1DA--FY27 NRM - EHRM Base 573-27-702-DB EHRM Generator Upgrades Design-Build - Gainesville VAMC
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC) is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of performing a Design-Build (DB) project. Services to include Architect and Engineering (DB A/E) design services, site preparation and DB Construction (DB C) services for the construction of Emergency Power Generator Upgrade for Electronic Health Record Modernization at the Malcom Randall VA Medical Center (VAMC) located in Gainesville, Florida. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Malcom Randall VA Medical Center (Gainesville VAMC) has a requirement to design and construct an Emergency Power Generator Upgrade to support Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) at the Malcom Randall VA Medical Center. This Design-Build Team (DBT) shall provide all design and construction services, investigations, labor, materials, equipment, supervision, transportation, permits, temporary emergency power, demolition, lawful disposal, site improvements, testing, commissioning, training, and documentation necessary to deliver a complete turnkey Emergency Power Generator Upgrade for EHRM at MRVAMC. The DBT shall evaluate existing conditions and deliver a code-compliant operational emergency power system while protecting the existing Emergency Power Switchboard and maintaining required hospital emergency power capability throughout construction, subject only to specifically approved planned switching windows. The facility's existing 1,275 kW emergency generator (Generator #5) reportedly operates at approximately 85% load; the Contractor shall independently verify actual demand and operating conditions. Planned EHRM infrastructure is estimated to add 150-200 kW of critical load, including IDF/telecommunications closets and associated cooling; the Hybrid OR project is estimated to add approximately 100 kW of emergency loads. These figures are planning estimates, not verified design loads. The replacement generator shall be rated at not less than 2,000 kW and selected to provide at least 10% unused rated kW capacity after accounting for verified coincident operating demand, planned loads, and site derating. The DBT shall provide a complete enclosed generator and all required fuel, exhaust, switchgear interface, ATS, distribution, monitoring, platform, site, and temporary emergency power work. Existing generator site boundaries are constrained; significant expansion to the north or south is not anticipated to be feasible. The DBT shall confirm the usable footprint and design a solution accordingly. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-build approach outlined in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 36.101-2, Use of two-phase design-build selection procedures. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. This project is planned for advertising in mid-January 2026. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $5,000.000.00 and $10,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 238210 (size standard $19.0 million) applies to this procurement. The duration of the project is currently estimated at 730 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all design and construction related services. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide company name, DUNS number and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 238210. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a statement of interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAPM Magnitude of Construction listed above. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: Provide a maximum of three (3) projects completed within the last ten years (10) years in which the Offeror s design-build team has worked together on previous design-build contracts similar in size, magnitude, complexity, and scope to this project. Projects must demonstrate a respondent s design-build experience as a prime construction contractor directly responsible to the owner and managing multiple subcontractors. NOTE: If a prime contractor does not have Design-Build experience, they are permitted to provide up to three (3) relevant non-Design-Build projects that are completed in clinical, hospital or other medical related use space similar in size, magnitude, complexity, and scope to this project. The designer for the team may also provide up to three (3) relevant projects that fall under the requested criteria for the project. A maximum total of six (6) projects may be submitted between the D-B and design teams. *All submission requirements for these projects remain the same and are listed above. Describe your Self-Performed** effort (as either a Prime or Subcontractor). Describe Self-Performed work in terms of dollar value and description. **Self-Performed means work performed by the offeror themselves, NOT work performed by another company for them for any of the project examples provided. It is requested that interested contractors submit a response (electronic submission) of no more than twelve (12) single sided pages, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum that addresses the above information. This response must be submitted as a single application-generated (not scanned) PDF document that is less than or equal to 4MB in size. Please note that hard copies will not be accepted. Please also include a cover page, which includes, at a minimum: the company s name, address, Unique Entity Identifier (if available), socio-economic status, point-of-contact name, phone number, and e-mail address. Responses must include the Sources Sought number and project title in the subject line of their e-mail response. Submissions (responses) shall be submitted via email to the primary and secondary points of contact listed below by December 7, 2026, at 2:00 PM ET. No phone calls will be accepted. The Capabilities Statement submitted in response to this Sources Sought shall not be considered to be a bid or proposal. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and is neither to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to the respondents. After completing its analyses, the Government will determine whether to limit competition among the small business categories listed above or proceed with full and open competition as other than small business. At this time no solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the solicitation. If a solicitation is released it will be synopsized in Contract Opportunities at https://sam.gov/.
